text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- "Time for action rather than words", King Hussein tells Netanyahu. "Unilateral changes to Arab Jerusalem are not acceptable".
- King Hussein receives Netanyahu, stresses need to adhere to agreements and not to affect current "status quo" in Jerusalem.
- 300 engineers out of many unemployed will soon leave to Malaysia for work.

- King stresses to Netanyahu the need to move to implement agreements and take action. Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti and Egyptian Foreign Minister review latest political developments and measures in Jerusalem.
- South African President Nelson Mandela to visit Jordan on November 19.
- King Hussein: "I am sad and upset and do not know how much more Palestinians can take."
- Drug smuggling cases increase by 400 per cent.
- Jordan's Businessmen Association reject idea of creating regional council (with Israel, PLO and Egypt) and says Israel has to adhere to agreements.
